text: 🍿 Carrie ends with a door open to a bigger King world /Film argues that Mike Flanagan has quietly soft-launched a second King universe. His 'Carrie' moves the story to the social media era and writes the bullies as people, not cartoons. Then it frames Carrie White as one link in a long line of psychic women. That's the smart part. A shared universe built on a lineage of powers beats stitching Easter eggs together, which is how 'The Dark Tower' (2017) sank. Flanagan already proved with 'Doctor Sleep' (2019) that he can honor King and still go his own way. Eight episodes on Prime Video, with Summer H. Howell and Samantha Sloyan. Flanagan's dream is three seasons, and no second season is confirmed yet. ✈️ Add to watchlist

🎬 Bay and Spielberg go back to Cybertron Michael Bay is in talks to direct the next Transformers for Paramount, with Steven Spielberg overseeing the franchise's creative direction again. Bay hasn't touched it since 'The Last Knight' (2017), and the Skydance-era Paramount is clearly betting on nostalgia as a reset button. 🤖 Honestly, it intrigues me and it worries me. After the grounded charm of 'Bumblebee' , going back to Bay's pyrotechnic maximalism feels like a step backward. But Spielberg as the adult in the room might be what keeps the explosions pointed at a story. Show me a script before I cheer.
